title: Closed support of proper pushforward lies in image
statement: Let Z be Noetherian, q : Y → Z proper, and F coherent on Y. If C is a closed subset equal to the support of F, then the support of q_*F is a closed subset D of Z contained in q(C).

source.place: Theorem 088E, support of H paragraph; Tag 02O5

proof.text: Properness and the locally Noetherian target make Y locally Noetherian. Apply the coherent/quasi-coherent finite-type equivalence to F. To supply finite presentation for the higher-direct-image theorem, choose finite local generators, reindex their indices by ULift (Fin n), and apply the kernel clause of coherence. The already proved isFinitePresentation_of_generators_kernel helper in CoherentFiniteTypeLocallyNoetherian gives presentations on this cover; Mathlib locality descends them. This is written in Lean as a generic local argument to avoid expensive unfolding of the concrete scheme sheaf in elaboration.

Use the existing Grothendieck-abelian instance for Y.Modules to obtain injective resolutions. In degree zero apply isFinitePresentation_higherDirectImage and isQuasicoherent_higherDirectImage. The pushforward is left exact, so Mathlib rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf identifies its degree-zero right derived functor with the ordinary pushforward. Transport finite presentation and quasi-coherence along this isomorphism.

Finite presentation implies finite type. Apply finite_type_module_support_closed to the ordinary pushforward and use its last conjunct as the closedness proof for D, whose underlying set is exactly the set of points with nonsubsingleton stalk.

Properness makes q a closed map. For x outside q(C), let V be the open complement of q(C). For every open U contained in V and y in its inverse image, y is outside C; the support equality hC therefore makes the stalk F_y subsingleton. By section_ext, all sections of F on the inverse image of U agree. Thus every section module of q_*F on an open contained in V is subsingleton.

Represent any two pushforward stalk elements at x by germs on opens U and W contained in V using exists_le_germ_eq. Their restrictions to U intersect W agree by the preceding subsingleton result. Twice apply germ_res_apply to identify their germs. Hence the stalk is subsingleton outside q(C); contraposition proves D is contained in q(C). The argument works for empty opens and zero sheaves as well.

lean.statement:
theorem pushforward_support_closed_subset
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Z]
    (q : Y ⟶ Z) [IsProper q] (F : CoherentModules Y)
    (C : TopologicalSpace.Closeds Y)
    (hC : (C : Set Y) = {x : Y | ¬ Subsingleton (F.obj.presheaf.stalk x)}) :
    ∃ D : TopologicalSpace.Closeds Z,
      (D : Set Z) =
        {x : Z | ¬ Subsingleton (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).obj F.obj).presheaf.stalk x)} ∧
      (D : Set Z) ⊆ q '' (C : Set Y)
